findings.description: The data bucket stores customer data without server-side encryption enabled. Any data stored here is stored in plaintext at rest, exposing confidential customer information if the underlying storage is accessed.

The data bucket is configured to be public (as noted in the comment) with no bucket policy or ACL restricting access to specific principals. This exposes the bucket and its contents to the entire internet, allowing anyone to read or modify stored data.

The data_object uploads a 'customer-master.xlsx' file containing customer data into a publicly accessible bucket with no encryption at rest. Customer information is exposed to unauthenticated access and stored in plaintext.

The financials bucket stores financial data without server-side encryption enabled. Financial records are stored in plaintext at rest, exposing sensitive financial information if the underlying storage is compromised.

The operations bucket is not configured with server-side encryption, so operational data is stored in plaintext at rest despite having versioning enabled. This exposes data confidentiality if the underlying storage is accessed.
The data_science bucket has versioning and logging enabled but no server-side encryption configuration. Data stored here is in plaintext at rest, exposing it if the underlying storage is compromised.

Data science bucket relies on a plaintext log target. Without encryption enabled, the bucket inherits no at-rest protection, and the logging block references a target bucket via interpolation that does not itself remediate data exposure.
